name: Phishing
description: Deceptive emails and messages designed to steal sensitive information.
how_it_works: An attacker sends a message that looks like it came from a trusted company or coworker. It pushes you to click a link or open a file, which then steals your passwords or installs harmful software.
how_we_defend: We filter suspicious email, add multi-factor logins so a stolen password is not enough, and train your team to spot fake messages.

name: Malware
description: Malicious software that can damage systems, steal data, or gain unauthorized access.
how_it_works: Malware gets onto a device through bad downloads, infected attachments, or out-of-date software. Once inside, it can spy on activity, steal files, or damage the system.
how_we_defend: We install endpoint protection, keep software updated, and watch devices for strange behavior so infected machines are caught and cleaned quickly.

name: Ransomware
description: Attacks that lock your data or system until ransom is paid.
how_it_works: Ransomware scrambles your files so you cannot open them, then demands payment for the key. Many attacks also steal a copy of the data and threaten to leak it.
how_we_defend: We keep secure offline backups, limit what each account can access, and have a response plan ready so you can restore your data without paying.

name: Insider Threats
description: Risks that come from within an organization, whether intentional or accidental.
how_it_works: An employee or contractor may leak data on purpose, or make an honest mistake like sending a file to the wrong person or reusing a weak password.
how_we_defend: We give people access only to what they need, track unusual activity, and provide training that makes safe habits normal.

name: Cloud Threats
description: Vulnerabilities that target cloud environments and stored data.
how_it_works: Attackers look for cloud storage left open to the public, weak settings, or stolen logins, then use them to reach data stored online.
how_we_defend: We review your cloud settings, turn on strong logins and encryption, and monitor activity so mistakes in your setup are fixed fast.

name: DDoS Attacks
description: Overwhelming traffic designed to disrupt operations and take systems offline.
how_it_works: A DDoS attack floods a website or server with fake traffic from many computers at once, so real customers cannot get through.
how_we_defend: We use traffic filtering to block fake requests and have a plan to keep your service running while an attack is happening.

name: Social Engineering
description: Tricks that manipulate people into giving up access or information.
how_it_works: Instead of hacking a computer, the attacker hacks a person. They may call pretending to be IT support, or show up pretending to be a vendor, to get inside.
how_we_defend: We set clear steps for verifying requests, train staff to slow down and double-check, and run practice drills.

name: Password Attacks
description: Attempts to guess or steal passwords to break into accounts.
how_it_works: Attackers try common passwords, reuse lists of passwords stolen from other breaches, or guess thousands of combinations until one works.
how_we_defend: We require strong, unique passwords with a password manager and multi-factor login, and lock accounts that show repeated failed attempts.
